title: Three Keepers Vanished: How Did Their Story Change? | Curio Files
description:
In 1900, three keepers vanished from the Flannan Isles lighthouse. A supply ship, the first visitor's letter, the superintendent's inquiry, and a later poem left very different kinds of written evidence.

We follow Moore's letter, then compare it with the inquiry and the poem. What was a work record, what was an accident inference, and what was a literary scene? The men's fate remains unconfirmed. The untouched meal and overturned chair are not evidence of what the first visitor saw.

Sources checked on October 16, 2026. AI illustrations are narrative aids, with generic, non-portrait figures. No certain death scene is reenacted.

chapters.arrival-date: The supply ship gets no answer
chapters.slate-entry: The slate points eleven days back
chapters.west-recalled: A rope chest is gone on the west side
chapters.investigator-opinion: The inquiry offers its likeliest explanation
chapters.exhibit-first: The original letter goes on display

ht63.text: Relief keeper Moore arrived by supply ship. No usual flag flew ashore.

a2ec.text: The ship sounded its horn. Still no answer.

xng2.text: The captain fired a rocket. The lighthouse stayed silent.

3nwg.text: Two days later, Moore wrote a letter about the landing.

q7ay.text: Three days later, the superintendent went to the west landing.

i73f.text: Years later, another page described a table inside.

kxdb.text: What did Moore find? Who wrote that later scene?

xf7d.text: At the east landing, Moore jumped ashore first.

874p.text: The others stayed aboard to await Moore's report.

448s.text: Moore later wrote that he saw no keeper outside the lighthouse.

sspt.text: The yard gate and outer door were shut. His letter does not say either was locked.

4pa4.text: But inside, the kitchen door stood open.

5udf.text: Moore saw the stove: no fire had burned for days.

pec2.text: He checked each room. Every bed was empty.

iima.text: He stopped searching and ran back to the landing.

t4yn.text: At the boat, he told the others the entire house was empty.

ek7h.text: One of them went back with him to search the house again.

fkmm.text: What would they find in the lantern room?

cyaq.text: The lamp was cleaned, and its oil containers were full.

anms.text: Ducat, Marshall and MacArthur were missing.

v7kk.text: Another keeper was on sick leave, so MacArthur stood in.

c8s2.text: The captain asked for volunteers to stay after hearing the news.

bkys.text: That night, Moore and another keeper relit the lamp.

njtt.text: They searched the island but found none of the three men.

z4u3.text: Moore noted MacArthur's coat was left behind. Could it tell who left first?

7tig.text: The other two men's sea boots and oilskins were missing.

phjr.text: Moore knew what they wore outside, making those items important.

m6gi.text: He said they wore them only when going down near the landing.

3w38.text: Why MacArthur left his coat is unexplained. The records cannot order their departures.

h8mk.text: Moore's letter records completed work. Can the inquiry narrow the time?

cuxc.text: The inquiry mentions a slate absent from his letter, with readings to copy.

s7pw.text: The logbook's last entry was December 13.

s4hn.text: The report says a clock had stopped. Its face gave no date.

fgbf.text: But later observations remained on the slate.

ey9a.text: They include 9 a.m. pressure, temperature and wind on the 15th.

yt2k.text: It logged that morning's light-out time.

37tf.text: The pots were washed, and the kitchen was tidy.

igw7.text: Together, those chores led the inquiry to that afternoon.

7zvf.text: This is an inference from work, not an eyewitness account.

x5ik.text: A passing ship reported seeing no light at midnight on the 15th.

ds8v.text: But Muirhead said that news reached the Board only after the men were found missing.

3tt3.text: Shore observers also logged each night's view.

nxpd.text: But did not seeing it mean the lamp was out?

k8sw.text: The superintendent questioned the two boys who had watched from shore.

szic.text: He checked shore logs: missing the light was nothing new.

s9zp.text: Bad weather had hidden it for four or five nights in a row.

ufsf.text: The ship report and shore logs need separate readings.

r3ds.text: The time narrowed. Where on the island did they go?

s7g4.text: On the 29th, Muirhead landed to inspect the site himself.

qj6q.text: East-side ropes lay as they had after the last relief.

8hj7.text: On the west side, he found very different damage.

ijjn.text: The sea barred the landing. He reached the crane platform.

y4ag.text: That platform stood 70 feet above sea level.

tvjn.text: The rope chest sat higher, tucked in a rock cleft.

dwtd.text: It held landing and mooring ropes, plus a crane handle.

madp.text: The chest was about 110 feet above sea level.

efzu.text: That was the site's height, not a measured wave height.

dfa9.text: The rope chest was gone; coils lay near the cleft and crane.

gqqh.text: Were those ropes used that day?

a83d.text: When inspected, all coils were wound, none undone. That cannot tell whether anyone used them that day.

vn6y.text: The previous winter, the earlier crane had washed away.

eskw.text: The crane was intact, its jib lowered and secured to rock.

dvmg.text: Its drum cover remained tied. Nothing showed it was in use.

wc2e.text: Yet iron railings by the platform and path were twisted.

anru.text: A heavy boulder from above had moved down onto the path.

2d4b.text: Over 20 hundredweight, about a tonne, it said.

rvc2.text: Even the lifebuoy tied to the rail was gone. Had someone used it?

cbd8.text: That rail was about as high as the cleft holding the chest.

q5ct.text: Muirhead found the knot intact, with canvas still stuck to it.

i3cg.text: He concluded the sea had torn the lifebuoy from its mount.

7nu6.text: Could west-side damage explain the men's fate?

ecsy.text: On January 8, 1901, he set out his likeliest explanation.

e5pv.text: He thought the men went west to secure the rope chest and gear.

ek4w.text: Then a sudden wave swept over where they stood.

9jra.text: He thought the retreating water pulled them away.

6xq2.text: This was an inference from damage. Nothing proves that final moment.

v7k5.text: He also considered whether wind blew them away.

e8ux.text: West winds would push them toward higher ground.

33cn.text: He thought they could have crouched before the cliff edge.

hpye.text: So the wind direction did not support them being blown to sea.

e2rt.text: Years later, another writer added detail to the empty house.

i9ud.text: That first page was Gibson's lighthouse poem in a collection published in 1912.

jreq.text: In the poem, a meal sat untouched on the table.

uedh.text: In that same passage, a chair lay overturned.

tbuz.text: The poem suggests a hasty exit. Did the original records say so?

wdik.text: Moore's letter mentions neither meal nor overturned chair.

dt4e.text: The tidy kitchen was recorded then; it cannot reveal their last meal.

2kc7.text: Moore's original letter survives, ready to compare with the later poem.

3ncp.text: In 2026, National Records of Scotland first displayed it.

qv4y.text: Here, unresolved means the men's final fate. Some later details can be checked.

wpvq.text: Subscribe and trace where strange stories began.
